correctness.rationale: Exact conserved-simplex reduction gives I′=-beta I[I+R+(1-sigma)C]; I decreases and converges to zero. Stable R,C equations imply R/I->a=alpha/(mu+delta), C/I->c=delta*a/(mu+gamma), then I~1/(Kt). Stable convolution and defect equations yield R=a I+b I^2+O(I^3), C=c I+d I^2+O(I^3), with b,d displayed in RESULT.md. The cubic I′=-KI^2-LI^3+O(I^4) has integrable reciprocal remainder, giving finite orbit-dependent H. For both feedback laws g=I+O(I^2), so K,L coincide. The check independently recovered K=3 and L=(3-epsilon1)/2 for mu=alpha=delta=gamma=1, beta=2, sigma=1. I(0)=0 and sigma endpoints handled; no claim away from threshold.

value.rationale: A nonlinear nonhyperbolic threshold is intrinsically important for relaxation rates, and the exact feedback-invariant leading amplitude versus feedback-sensitive sign-reversing log coefficient distinguishes mechanisms not visible from linear stability. It is a substantial parameter-uniform asymptotic classification, not an arbitrary small-case computation.
